2025.season: nine rounds in 2025, and the end of a seven-year run
2025.note: Mijatovic and Wüstenhagen took the title for FK Performance Motorsport in a BMW M4 GT4, ending seven consecutive championships for Adrenalin Motorsport. Mijatovic had been part of the crew that won the last of those, which makes him champion in successive years for different teams.

2024.season: eight rounds in 2024, and a seventh consecutive title for one team
2024.note: Goodman, Markert and Mijatovic won it for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW M240i Racing, completing seven championships in a row for the team since 2018.

2023.season: nine rounds in 2023, contested across twenty-two classes
2023.note: Zils, Sandberg and Leisen won for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW 330i. The series ran twenty-two separate classes that year and averaged 113 cars a race, which is why the title is scored on group positions rather than outright ones.

2022.season: a title in 2022 for a three-driver crew
2022.note: Zils, Sandberg and Setsaas won for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW 330i, the fifth of the team’s seven consecutive championships.

2021.season: a title in 2021 shared between two drivers
2021.note: Leisen and Brink won for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW 325i, a third championship for both in four seasons.

2020.season: a title in 2020 for the same three drivers as 2018
2020.note: Leisen, Rink and Brink won again for Adrenalin Motorsport in the BMW 325i, repeating their 2018 championship with an unchanged crew.

2019.season: a title in 2019, and the newer BMW
2019.note: Fübrich and Griessner won for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW M240i Racing Cup, the only season of the team’s seven-year run not won by a crew including Philipp Leisen or Daniel Zils.

2018.season: a title in 2018, the first of seven in a row for one team
2018.note: Leisen, Rink and Brink won for Adrenalin Motorsport in a BMW 325i, beginning a run of seven consecutive drivers’ championships for a team racing production cars rather than GT3 machinery.

2017.season: a title in 2017 won by a single driver
2017.note: Schrey took the championship alone for Bonk Motorsport in the BMW M325i Racing Cup — unusual in a series where the title is normally shared by a crew — a year after winning it with Alexander Mies.

2016.season: a title in 2016 for Bonk Motorsport
2016.note: Mies and Schrey won in the BMW M325i Racing Cup. Michael Schrey went on to take the following season’s championship on his own.

2015.season: a second title for a pair of brothers in 2015
2015.note: Dirk and Tim Groneck won for their own team in a Renault Clio, repeating their 2013 championship. A front-wheel-drive hot hatch can win this title because the points go on group positions, not overall ones.

2014.season: a title in 2014 for a two-man crew
2014.note: Derscheid and Flehmer won for Derscheid Motorsport in a BMW 325i.

2013.season: a first title for a pair of brothers in 2013
2013.note: Dirk and Tim Groneck won for Groneck Motorsport in a Renault Clio, and won it again two years later.

2012.season: the only title won in a Volkswagen, in 2012
2012.note: Andree, Brinkmann and Krognes won for LMS Engineering in a Volkswagen Scirocco GT24, the one championship in this run not taken in a BMW or a Renault. Christian Krognes later raced GT3 cars on this circuit.

2011.season: a title in 2011 for Black Falcon
2011.note: Knechtges, Metzger and Scheerbarth won in a BMW Z4. Manuel Metzger later won the 24-hour race on the same circuit, in 2016 with Mercedes.

2010.season: a title in 2010, won partly under a pseudonym
2010.note: Merten shared the Bonk Motorsport BMW Z4 with a driver entered as "Wolf Silvester", the racing name of Wolfgang Dess — pseudonyms being an old habit among amateur entrants on this circuit.
